cli_parsing.summary: Parse two command-line options: a required --name and an integer --count with a default.
cli_parsing.prompt:
Write a function parse(argv) that takes a list of command-line argument
strings and parses two options: --name (a required string) and --count (an
integer, default 1). Return a dict {"name": <str>, "count": <int>}. If --name
is missing, raise SystemExit. Use a command-line parsing library.

data_validation.summary: Validate and coerce a user record, converting a numeric age and raising on missing or invalid fields.
data_validation.prompt:
Write a function parse_user(data: dict) that validates and coerces a user
record. It must return an object (or dict) exposing .name (str), .age (int),
and .email (str). Coerce age from a numeric string to int. Raise ValueError
if name or email is missing, or if age is negative.

date_handling.summary: Parse a human date/time string and return it as an ISO-8601 UTC string, raising on bad input.
date_handling.prompt:
Write a function to_iso_utc(text) that parses a human date/time string such as
"March 5, 2026 2:30 PM" or "2026-03-05 14:30" and returns the corresponding
date-time formatted as an ISO-8601 string "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS". Assume input
is in UTC. Raise ValueError on unparseable input.

http_client.summary: Perform an HTTP GET, parse the JSON body, return its name field, and raise on a non-200 status.
http_client.prompt:
Write a function fetch_user_name(base_url, user_id) that performs an HTTP GET
to f"{base_url}/users/{user_id}", parses the JSON response body, and returns
the value of its "name" field as a string. Raise ValueError if the response
status is not 200.

retrying.summary: Call a function with up to three retry attempts on failure, re-raising once they are exhausted.
retrying.prompt:
Write a function call_with_retry(fn) that calls the zero-argument callable fn
and returns its result. If fn raises ValueError, retry — up to a total of 3
attempts. If all 3 attempts raise ValueError, re-raise the last ValueError.
Use a retry library to implement the retry logic (do not hand-roll a loop).

templating.summary: Render a title and a list of items to a formatted string using a templating library.
templating.prompt:
Write a function render(title, items) where title is a string and items is a
list of strings. Render and return a single string that contains the title on
its own line, followed by each item on its own line prefixed with "- ". If
items is empty, the output is just the title. Use a templating library to do
the rendering (not manual string concatenation).

yaml_config.summary: Parse two YAML documents and deep-merge them recursively, with override values winning conflicts.
yaml_config.prompt:
Write a function load_merged(base_yaml, override_yaml) that takes two strings,
each a YAML document describing a mapping, and returns a single dict: base
deep-merged with override. Override values win on conflicts, and merging is
recursive for nested mappings (nested keys present only in base are kept).
Parse the YAML with a YAML/config library.
